column2: Blood for the Blood God!
Skulls for the Skull Throne!

Khorne's followers raise him no temples and burn him no incense. They worship him on the battlefield, and when there is no battle to be had they worship him by hacking at one another. The Blood God has no use for prayers, only for blood and for skulls, and his contempt for weaklings is boundless.\n\nTonight the dream came again: the Brass Citadel, the mountain of skulls, and on its summit a throne whose occupant did not deign to look at you. You are brave, but you are weak, and Khorne despises weakness. Kill until your arm is tired and your skin is stained red, or suffer the fate of the weak.
Who dies first?
Sacrifice some cattle instead...

While the worship of other gods needs rituals, altars and sacrifices, Khorne asks only that his followers spill fresh blood and take skulls in his name. A young warrior of [Root.Culture.GetName] blood has come to your hall with an axe in his fist and the Blood God's rune cut into his cheek. He wants your skull, and he says so before the whole court.
By Khorne, it will be done!
Sacrifice some cattle instead...

Khorne's berserkers are unstable warriors who revel in battle and live only for the shedding of blood in his name. Only those who give themselves utterly to the Lord of Skulls and heap a mountain of skulls before him become such warriors. One stands before you now, foam on his lips and a crust of other men's blood on his armour, ready to offer your skull to the Skull Throne.
For the slaughter!
I have already proven my worth...

You wear the skull of a servant of Khorne on your belt and boast that no mortal can best you. The Blood God has heard the boast. The air in your hall turns hot and stinks of brass and slaughter, the shadows run red, and a Bloodletter steps out of them: a daemon of Khorne, horned and grinning, with a hellblade that has drunk the blood of a thousand champions.
I am invincible!
You fight a duel to the death. Win, and take the skull.
[khorne_trial_foe.GetFirstName] is down in the blood and sawdust and cannot rise. The court holds its breath. A skull is a skull only once it has left the shoulders.
Your skull is mine!
Let [khorne_trial_foe.GetHerHim] live.

The fight is over, and [khorne_trial_foe.GetFirstName] still stands. Khorne cares not from whence the blood flows, but he cares very much that it flows, and today it did not flow enough. The dreams of the Brass Citadel do not come again.
Next time I will not miss.

You bellow your triumph over the third corpse so that Khorne himself might hear it, and he does. A white-hot pain shoots through your limbs and you fall to your knees, roaring. When you rise, your arms are thick as oak and you hold your axe like a hatchet. You have the strength of two men, and the Blood God's eye is on you.
My axe shall feast on the blood of my foes!
A Glorious Death!

The battle rages on around you, your warriors pressing forward in a frenzy as you lie bleeding on the ground. The world slows to a crawl, and your last moments are filled with cries of rage and anguish, the clash of steel and the spilling of blood. Then you see a figure high above the battle: a winged woman wreathed in flame and gore, with a blood-lust in her eyes more ravenous than any mortal's. Valkia the Bloody, the Gorequeen, has seen your death and has come to carry your soul to the halls of Khorne, where you shall be a handmaiden of the Blood God, second only to his Gorequeen herself!

Valkia the Bloody, the Gorequeen, has seen your death and has come to carry your soul to the halls of Khorne, where you shall fight against all who have fallen in the Blood God's service, for all eternity!
I go to the great fields of slaughter!
Crippled

Crippled, you begin to brood over your existence: how short life is, how little of it you may have left. But you are a lord, and strong, and you shake the fear from your mind. You are far too strong to be beaten by a setback such as this...
I will not let this beat me!
Denial

Your condition grows worse. Perhaps it is more serious than you first thought. Fear makes its home in your mind, and with it something else: a dark, warm, irrational presence, like the smell of a sickroom.
I can't die, not... like this...
Anger

There is still no sign of your condition improving, and your blood starts to boil. Surely someone is to blame for this. Everything you aspired to has been torn from you, and your life feels futile, a stagnant pool of resentment.
I was meant to live forever in glory! *cough* I was meant for so much more than this!
Bargaining
You cling to every scrap of strength you have left. Perhaps one of the gods still listens? What if you offered them gold, slaves, anything you own...
Gods... do not forsake me...
Despair
Your strength has deserted you and hope has abandoned you. All is lost. Too weak even to speak aloud, you lie and wonder how much time you have left.
Is this really how I am to die? Not with a roar, but with a whimper...
Acceptance?

You lie in your bed, ready to accept your fate and let go, when a gargling voice fills your mind, warm and kindly as a grandfather's. "Give yourself unto the Lord of Decay and you shall feel no more pain, nor fear death ever again. All things die, little one, all things rot, and in the rot there is life! Who but Grandfather Nurgle can protect you from the rot? Who but the Lord of Decay knows the true gift of immortality?"
Plaguefather... deliver me from this existence!
No. I am ready for this to end...
Plaguelord

As the oath passes your lips, the pain seeps out of your body. In its place you are filled with joy, with power, with a warmth that spreads from your belly to your fingertips: a warmth you long to share with the whole world. Your flesh blisters and weeps and you do not mind at all. The Grandfather loves you.
I will bring you glory, my Lord.
Acceptance
You have turned your back on the Grandfather's gift. Now you close your eyes and wait for the end, and for the first time in months you feel at peace.
I am prepared to meet my ancestors...
Inspiration

The world is so vast and so confusing, and there is so much left to understand, that the very thought of grasping it sinks you into a pit of hopelessness. Then one night the Architect of Fate reaches into your addled mind, and for a few heartbeats you see the threads: every fate, every choice, every change, glittering in the dark like the walls of the Crystal Labyrinth. Then they are gone, and you are left with a headache and a terrible hunger to see them again.
I will carefully study these visions...
I would risk everything to know the infinite!
I fear the power of change...
Boon of Tzeentch

Ignorance is a disease that swallows the content and the fearful, and through the Changer's gifts you see it now. Your mind is set aflame with knowledge beyond your years, and the fire drives you to seek out more, to grasp at the endless threads of your destiny and learn where each of them might lead...
I must adapt and grow...

Lately you have spent long, sensual nights talking with [darkprince_daemonette.GetFirstNameWithNick], your 'loyal' daemonette. You have spoken at length of the Dark Prince, of the gardens of delight that lie just beyond this world, and of how you should stop trying to master your desires. Would it not be far better to let your desires master you? Deeper into this realm of wonder and temptation there is a path you could walk... together...
I will need a fresh supply of slaves to practise on...
Your old virtue may yet hold.
Only fools and pawns drown themselves in excess!
The Lord of Pleasure

Boredom has begun to plague you. A life of excess and carnal pleasure seems less fulfilling with every passing night, and even the exquisite bite of cold steel against your skin no longer stirs you. Then, one night, cruel and sensual echoes tug at the edge of your mind, teasing you with forbidden thoughts that leave you aching for something more. Somehow you know what this path requires: a rite, a circle, and a great many things your cult will have to gather for you.
A couple of hundred lashes to spur my servants first...
These are a madman's dreams. I will not listen.

Your cult has gathered everything you need. The signs are right, and the Winds of Magic blow so wild here that your rite tears easily through the thin veil between the worlds. Or perhaps someone was tearing through from the other side. A pair of unearthly eyes glows at you through the rent in reality, and a voice like honey and broken glass laughs your name.
Come forth, dark angel, and give me your name!
Close it! Close it now!

For days I have burned and shivered and coughed up things I would rather not name. Then, in the worst of the fever, I heard a deep and kindly laugh, smelled sweet rot and felt a great soft hand on my brow. The sickness is still in me, but it no longer hurts. Grandfather Nurgle has blessed my suffering, and I feel more alive than I ever did before!
Thank you, Grandfather!

Since the change came upon my flesh, the same nobles who once bowed to me make the sign against evil behind my back. In the villages they burn mutants alive for less than I bear. The people I once called friends and kin look at me with disgust. Somewhere deep in my blood, a voice is growing louder, and it says they should all be made to pay.
Gather the mutants and let the city burn!
Perhaps they are right to fear what I am.
I will not question the will of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap].
My courage is known throughout the realm, but of late there has been nothing to test it against. Peace makes men soft. I lie awake at night with my hand on my sword, aching for an enemy worth facing.

My strength is known throughout the realm, but of late there has been no one to test it against. Peace makes men soft. I lie awake at night with my hand on my sword, aching to break something that fights back.
I have won more duels to first blood than I can count, and every time, as my opponent yields, I want to see more blood. First blood is not enough any more. It has not been enough for a long time.
I will find a worthy foe and fight!
I have nothing to prove.
[Root.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap] gives me all the courage I need.

My body is a map of every battle I have fought. Each scar is a badge of honour, proof that I took the blow and still stand. But the scars are fading, and the courtiers no longer stare. I find myself running a knife along my arm, wondering how deep a cut must go to leave a mark worth having.
More scars! Let the blood flow!
My scars speak for themselves.
[Root.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap] protects me.

I have hunted stag, boar, bear and wolf, and none of them is a challenge any more. The beasts run and die. I want a quarry that thinks, that hides, that fights back. A quarry that knows what is coming.
I will hunt the most dangerous game of all.
Maybe I should find another pastime.
[Root.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap] gives and takes away.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] invited me on a hunting trip. Deep in the forest, the huntsmen fell back one by one, and [From.GetTitledFirstName] smiled and told me to run. I am the quarry.
Run!

The heads on the pikes above my gate have rotted down to bare skulls, and I find I like them better that way: clean, white, grinning. There are not nearly enough of them to line the walls the way I see them in my dreams.
The peasants have skulls they are not using.
A new statue of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap] would look better.
I must pray. These dreams are not mine.

Any general knows it is better to make the enemy die for his lord than to die for yours. My men do not understand this. They fight like farmers. If only they fought each other once in a while, the weak would be culled and the strong would learn what it means to win.
Make them fight each other to the death!
There must be another way.
[Root.Religion.GetRandomGodNameCap] will guide me.
A servant laughed at my face today, loudly, in the great hall, and said it was a wonder the mutant riots had not burned the rest of me too. Half the court heard. The voice in my blood is roaring.
A servant openly wondered in the hall whether my famous duel ever happened, or whether I bought the bards. Half the court heard. The voice in my blood is roaring.

While I was admiring my new scars in the glass, I heard a courtier say that my face looks like a butcher's floor, and that the butcher should be ashamed. Half the court laughed. The voice in my blood is roaring.

A guest at dinner asked, loud enough for the whole table, whether I had killed any of the trophies on my walls myself or bought them from the huntsmen. Half the court laughed. The voice in my blood is roaring.
A guest remarked over dinner that skulls on the walls are terribly out of fashion and frighten the ladies. Half the court laughed. The voice in my blood is roaring.
A servant threw himself at my feet in the hall, weeping and wailing, begging me to spare his brother from the war games. The whole court is watching what I will do. The voice in my blood is roaring.
Put his head on a pike!
Fight him to the death, here and now!
Kill him in his sleep.
He does not know any better. Let him be.

Weakness. All I see around me is weakness and corruption. Peace breeds excess, and only war is pure. Every day I long for the clash of arms, for fresh blood splattered across my face, for my enemies' homes in flames and their warriors in flight. Better that than whining, ungrateful vassals and the false counsel of effete scholars and sorcerers. Kill them. Kill them all. Khorne, Lord of the Skull Throne, calls me to his service, and I answer.
BLOOD FOR THE BLOOD GOD! SKULLS FOR THE SKULL THRONE!
You serve the Blood God in secret.
